To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the NMR spectra of the oxidized and reduced forms of the [2Fe--2S] ferredoxin from the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium, Anabaena 7210 are quite similar; (2) the NMR data are consistent with an alpha-beta-beta-alpha fold; (3) a number of the residues that are closest to the iron-sulfur center are not seen in the NMR spectra.
the secondary structure of the protein in solution is very similar to the secondary structure determined by X-ray crystallography and that the protein is very well folded in solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function and evolution of the [2Fe2S] ferredoxin family of proteins.
the study of the structural and dynamical properties of proteins by means of NMR spectroscopy.

the study of the structure of proteins in solution using NMR spectroscopy, and in particular, we are interested in the study of proteins that bind to nucleic acids and in the study of protein folding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper describes the first successful attempt at obtaining sequence specific assignments of the diamagnetic resonances of a protein that is a member of a family that contains many paramagnetic members.
the 3-dimensional structure of the oxidised form of Anabaena heterocyst ferrodoxin is similar to those of other [2Fe-25]-ferredoxins.

the NMR studies of the oxidized heterocyst ferreoxin from Anabena 7120 have shown that it is a protein of 102 amino acids, which is a homodimer in solution and has a well-defined secondary structure, which is in good agreement with the X-ray structure of the reduced form of the protein.

this paper is the first example of using a triple-resonance experiment to assign protein backbone resonances, and it is also the first example of the use of a triple-resonanance experiment to determine secondary structure in proteins.
the NMR spectra of heterocyst ferrodoxin were assigned and the secondary structure of the protein was elucidated.
we were able to obtain a complete sequence-specific resonance assignment and secondary structure for Anabaena heterocyst ferrodoxin.
